title: Maratha river navy: the secret fleet that shocked the British
hook: A hidden Maratha fleet slipped past British warships in 1754, rewriting naval history.
description:
A hidden Maratha fleet slipped past British warships in 1754, rewriting naval history. Discover how this secret river navy altered the balance of power and why it vanished after Balaji's death.

Subscribe for more untold stories of empire's hidden weapons.
#marathaempire #history #navalhistory #historyfacts #shorts

beats.say: Imagine a hidden Maratha fleet silently slipping past British warships in 1754, defying naval supremacy.
beats.visual: Maratha fleet sailing near British warships 1754

beats.say: Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao secretly hired European shipwrights to build swift, shallow-draft vessels for river raids.
beats.visual: European shipwrights constructing Maratha river vessels

beats.say: These craft navigated the Godavari's twisting channels, striking the Portuguese at Surat in a surprise night assault.
The raid captured 200,000 rupees in silver, funding the Maratha cavalry's rapid expansion across the Deccan.
British admiral George Pocock called it 'the most audacious inland naval operation ever witnessed,' fearing a new frontier.
Yet the Marathas never built a formal navy; the fleet was disbanded after Balaji's death in 1761.
Historians once thought the Maratha navy was myth, but recent archives at Pune reveal detailed ship logs.
beats.visual: Archive documents Pune Maratha ship logs

beats.say: These logs show a 12-month campaign, coordinating with land forces to cut British supply lines along the coast.
The episode proved Maratha ingenuity could challenge European sea power without a standing fleet.
Today, the forgotten river navy reminds us that empire's strength lay in daring tactics, not just armies.
